findings.codeql_raw_query:
/**
 * @name Unsafe file operations in tomlkit
 * @description Detects use of built-in open() and os file APIs that may be security-relevant when used on untrusted paths.
 * @kind problem
 * @problem.severity warning
 * @id py/tomlkit/unsafe-file-ops
 * @tags security
 *       external/cwe/cwe-022
 */

import python
import semmle.python.ApiGraphs
import semmle.python.dataflow.new.DataFlow

from DataFlow::CallCfgNode call
where
  call.getLocation().getFile().getRelativePath().matches("tomlkit/%") and
  (
    call = API::builtin("open").getACall() or
    call = API::moduleImport("os").getMember(["open", "remove", "unlink", "rmdir", "removedirs"]).getACall()
  )
select call, "File operation that may be security-relevant depending on how paths are provided to tomlkit."
findings.hypothesis: tomlkit may perform file operations on attacker-controlled paths leading to path traversal or unsafe file access.

message.text: File operation that may be security-relevant depending on how paths are provided to tomlkit.

findings.codeql_raw_query:
/**
 * @name tomlkit file operations overview
 * @description Identify file reads/writes in tomlkit to assess security impact of path handling.
 * @kind problem
 * @problem.severity warning
 * @id py/tomlkit/unsafe-file-ops
 * @tags security
 *       external/cwe/cwe-022
 */

import python
import semmle.python.ApiGraphs
import semmle.python.dataflow.new.DataFlow

from DataFlow::CallCfgNode call, string filename
where
  call.getLocation().getFile().getRelativePath() = "tomlkit/toml_file.py" and
  (
    call = API::moduleImport("builtins").getMember("open").getACall() or
    call = API::moduleImport("io").getMember("open").getACall() or
    call = API::moduleImport("pathlib").getMember("Path").getMember(["open", "read_text", "write_text"]).getACall()
  ) and
  exists(DataFlow::ExprNode arg | arg = call.getArg(0) | filename = arg.toString())
select call, "File operation that may be security-relevant depending on how paths are provided to tomlkit."
findings.hypothesis: tomlkit performs file operations whose paths may be influenced by untrusted input, potentially enabling path traversal or unintended file access when used in higher-level applications.

message.text: File operation that may be security-relevant depending on how paths are provided to tomlkit.
